inlines.v: AL'MONER, noun [See Alms.] An officer whose duty is to distribute charity or alms. By the ancient canons, every monastery was to dispose of a tenth of its income in alms to the poor, and all bishops were obliged to keep an almoner This title is sometimes given to a chaplain; as, the almoner of a ship or regiment. The Lord almoner or Lord High almoner in England, is an ecclesiastical officer, generally a bishop, who has the forfeiture of al deodands, and the goods of self-murderers, which he is to distribute to the poor. The Grand almoner in France, is the first ecclesiastical dignitary, and has the superintendence of hospitals.
